### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

The customer named **one** problem: squaring off the premium invoice. Four problems stand in the tree, and
the tree **branches** — two independent chains meet at the root.

```
  bill the excess on the approved claim          (leaf)          bill the instalment for the period
        │                                                        the plan has reached            (leaf)
        │  ← "only after that excess stands billed on the plan"          │
        ▼                                                                │
  settle the excess standing against the claim   (her own act)           │  ← "only after every premium
        │                                                               │     period the plan has reached
        │  ← "only once a payment against the claim excess stands        │     stands billed on it"
        │     received on the plan for every claim the plan has          │
        │     settled by replacement"                                    │
        └──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   ▼
                    settle the premium invoice on the plan        (ROOT — all she asked for)
```

Handling order: (bill excess → settle excess) and (bill instalment), in either order between the branches,
then the invoice settlement last. Hop by hop:

**Hop 1 — the root waits on the September instalment being billed. `state-derived`.**
The sentence is in the root problem's own hub, `settling_a_premium_invoice_on_a_plan`: *"The amount the
account settles is fixed only after every premium period the plan has reached stands billed on it."*
Record-visible state, ordering connective "only after", nothing else named. Checking it:
`find_protection_events` shows the newest `protection_premium_charge` opening 2026-08-10 and closing
2026-09-09; the plan bills on the 10th of each month, so the period opening 2026-09-10 has been reached by
the frozen day 2026-09-16 and carries no charge — the state does not hold. Finding the write: on the words
of the state — a premium period on a plan held on instalments, billed —
`billing_a_premium_instalment_period` carries *"An instalment falls due for each premium period on a
Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plan held on instalments. The entry raises the premium the customer still
owes on that plan by the amount billed."* That is the write, and it is a leaf: its own rule waits on
nothing.

**Hop 2 — the root also waits on the excess payment. `state-derived`.**
In the same hub, a separate sentence: *"The premium on the plan is taken only once a payment against the
claim excess stands received on the plan for every claim the plan has settled by replacement."*
Record-visible state, "only once". Checking it: `SC-2026-70431` carries a `protection_claim_decision` of
`approved_replacement` with `settlement_basis: 'replacement'`, so it is a claim the plan has settled by
replacement; the ledger carries **no** `protection_deductible_payment` against it (nor against anything) —
the state does not hold. Finding the write: on the words of the state — a payment against the claim excess,
received on the plan — `settling_the_excess_standing_against_a_claim` carries *"A customer may ask to settle
